about: Hard invariants for drawing SysML v2 diagrams. These are the rules a diagram violates or it does not — the equivalent of the textual prompting rules, but for pictures. Each rule states what to draw, why the notation requires it, a correct and a wrong form, and whether a machine can check it (and how). Evidence is a figure from the OMG SysML v2 reference implementation or one of this repo's own renders.
conventions: ✅ correct · ❌ wrong · ⚠️ gotcha. Rule ids are stable (D1, D2, …) so a checklist can cite them. `checkable` values: `ir` (a machine check exists against the notation IR / emitted .tex), `geometry` (checkable from box and port coordinates), `visual` (needs a human or a vision model).

rules.statement: Draw a definition with SQUARE corners and a usage with ROUNDED corners.
rules.why: The keyword line is small; the corner is visible at a glance and is the reference implementation's only reliable shape-level tell.
rules.correct:
«part def» Vehicle — square box
«part» vehicle_b : Vehicle — rounded box
rules.wrong: both boxes drawn the same shape, so the reader must zoom to tell a type from a role
rules.check: def nodes use the square-corner macro, usage nodes the rounded one

rules.statement: A definition's header is its name; a usage's header is `name : Type`. Put the type in the header, never in a compartment row.
rules.why: Typing a usage is what makes it a usage of something; a row cannot express it and readers will not find it.
rules.check: usage nodes carry a non-empty type

rules.statement: Every box carries its keyword line inside it, in guillemets, italic: «part», «attribute def», «requirement». Do not rely on the reader inferring it from context.
rules.why: Without the keyword a box is ambiguous: the same rectangle is a part, an item or an occurrence depending on one word.
rules.check: every node's kind is rendered as a keyword line

rules.statement: Separate compartments with a full-width rule and title each with an italic centred noun. On definitions use the bare noun (`attributes`, `ports`, `parts`); on usages use verb + noun (`perform actions`, `exhibit states`).
rules.why: The compartment title says what kind of membership the rows express; a bare noun on a usage hides that the rows are performed or exhibited.
rules.correct:
attributes / parts / ports on a definition
perform actions / exhibit states on a usage
rules.wrong: one undivided box of rows, or `actions` on a usage
rules.check: compartment labels follow the definition/usage table

rules.statement: Express relationships in rows with the notation's own operators: `:>` subsetting, `:>>` redefinition, `=` binding, `default` for a default value, `[n]`/`[n..m]` for multiplicity. Never draw an arrow to say what a row says.
rules.why: Those operators are the model's semantics; an arrow between two rows cannot carry `:>>` and invents a connection the model does not have.

rules.statement: Draw a port as a small square straddling the box border, with the port name outside the box beside it. Show direction with a small chevron inside the square (`in` / `out`), not with an arrowhead on the connector.
rules.why: A port is a feature of the boundary, not an icon on the box; and in an interconnection view connectors carry no arrowheads, so the chevron is the only direction signal.
rules.correct: □ on the border, `fuelIn` written outside, `←` inside the square
rules.wrong: port drawn as a dot inside the box, or direction shown by an arrowhead on the connector
rules.check: every port glyph centre lies within 2pt of its box wall

rules.statement: Put the filled diamond at the WHOLE end. The part end gets no arrowhead and no diamond.
rules.why: The diamond marks ownership; putting it on the part end inverts the model, and readers take the diamond end as the owner.
rules.wrong:
Vehicle ———◆ Engine   (ownership inverted)
Vehicle ◆———▶ Engine (diamond plus arrowhead)
rules.check: composition edges route to the whole node with the diamond style and no extra arrowhead

rules.statement: Place a multiplicity at the end it quantifies: at the part end when the part is the many side, at the whole end when the whole is (as in a usage composed of one definition).
rules.why: A multiplicity floating near the middle reads as belonging to the relationship, not to an end.
rules.check: labels on composition edges are attached as end labels, not mid-edge labels

rules.statement: Draw specialisation as a solid line with a HOLLOW triangle at the general type. One triangle may serve several subclasses joined by a bus.
rules.why: Filled triangles mean flow; a filled triangle here makes a type hierarchy look like a data flow.
rules.check: generalisation edges use the hollow-triangle style

rules.statement: Give a requirement an id in angle brackets in its name line, and use `doc`, `attributes` and `constraints` compartments. Write `assume` and `require` in bold inside `constraints`.
rules.why: Requirements are read by reviewers looking for text and thresholds; prose in an untitled compartment is unreadable as a requirement.
rules.correct:
«requirement»
<1> vehicleMassRequirement : MassRequirement
  doc  …
  attributes  massRequired = 2000 [kg]
  constraints  assume { fuelMassActual == fuelMassMax }
rules.wrong: «requirement» VehicleMass  {The vehicle shall weigh less than 2000 kg}
rules.check: requirement nodes carry an id and a doc/attributes compartment

rules.statement: Draw satisfy / verify / derive / allocate / perform / expose / import as DASHED or DOTTED edges carrying the keyword in guillemets as the label.
rules.why: These are not structural connections; drawing them solid makes them indistinguishable from composition and connector edges.
rules.check: cross-cutting edges use a dashed style and a keyword label

rules.statement: When a diagram is enclosed in a frame, the header names the view kind (`ibd`, `act`, `stm`) or the owning element (`«part» vehicle_b : Vehicle`). A frame header describes the container, never the boxes inside.
rules.why: fig-67 is headed «use case» yet contains actions — the header says what the diagram is a view of. Agents that classify by header alone mislabel the contents.
rules.correct:
«part» vehicle_b : Vehicle  →  contents are parts and ports
«view» Vehicle States : State Transition View  →  contents are states

rules.statement: Use only SysML v2 marks. No crow's feet, no ERD multiplicities, no UML-style `*` for many, no activity pins, no stick figures inside a block.
rules.why: Borrowed notation reads as a different language; a crow's foot in a SysML diagram is a defect, not a dialect.
rules.correct: 1 / 0..* / [1..4] as text labels at edge ends
rules.wrong: —< (crow's foot), * (UML many), ● inside a box for a pin
rules.evidence: all corpus figures use text multiplicities

rules.statement: Do not present a specification (metamodel) figure as a diagram of a system. If the boxes carry bold class names, hollow triangles and `+/role 0..* {subsets …}` labels, it defines the language.
rules.why: Metamodel figures share the visual vocabulary but answer a different question; quoting one as a system design is a category error.
rules.correct:
(in a design review) a parts tree, interconnection or flow
(in the specification) ControlNode ◁— ForkNode
rules.wrong: using fig-33's TransitionUsage ladder to explain how a vehicle changes state
